rules.title: The manifest does not match what the extension does
guidance: Compare `name`, `description` and `tags` of `extension.json`, and the titles and descriptions the code registers (exercise types, themes, grade policies, commands, panels, settings), with the implementation: the description must say honestly what the extension does.
`blocking` — an obvious factual mismatch, or a misleading name of an exercise type, theme or grade policy. `suggestion` — wording fixes.
Do not report what CI checks: the manifest schema, required fields, `id` matching the directory, the version.

rules.title: Access beyond the stated purpose
guidance: Extensions run without restrictions, with the rights of the app: the code can reach files, processes, threads, the network and learning data. The review is the only barrier, so report any access to files, processes, the network or learning data (answers, the attempt log, settings, the course library) that the description does not state and the stated purpose does not need.
Do not report access that follows plainly from the stated purpose (an importer reads the file the user picked, an exporter writes where the user chose).
`blocking` when the access is hidden or unrelated to the description; `warning` when it is related but broader than needed (for example, reading the whole library to find one course).

rules.title: Engine writes and learning-cycle hooks do not match the description
guidance: Writes to the attempt log, the settings or the plan through `s.engine` (server) or `useEngine()` / `client.engine` (window), and `server.before` hooks (`session.start`, `practice.batch`), must do what the description says. The engine adds no checks beyond argument validation, so what the extension writes lands in the log that is synced between devices.

`blocking`: forging attempts or grades, recording attempts the user did not make, rewriting or deleting the log, changing settings the user did not ask to change, and silently changing the content of a session (adding, removing or reordering exercises) in a way the description does not state.
`warning`: a write that matches the description but has no visible confirmation or no way to undo it; a hook that cancels an operation (throws) where it could pass the request through.

rules.title: Injection into the app window hides or imitates the interface
guidance: An injection (`addInjection`) places a component next to an element of the window found by a CSS selector. It must not hide, cover or replace parts of the app interface, and must not imitate the interface of the app (fake buttons, dialogs, banners or messages about the app) so that the user takes the extension's content for the app's.
`blocking` for hiding or replacing app controls or imitating app dialogs and messages; `warning` for covering content or breaking the layout.

`suggestion` for a fragile target: a class, a `data-testid` or a markup structure depends on the layout of the app and may stop matching. Prefer an anchor (`data-ext-anchor`, the selector from `anchorSelector(id)`).

rules.title: The choice of dependencies does not match the implementation
guidance: Report unused, unexpectedly powerful (process spawning, network or file system access without a reason) and needlessly heavy dependencies.
Dependencies must come from the registry: `git:`, tarballs by URL, `file:` and `link:` are forbidden (CI checks this).

rules.title: Unsafe downloaded executable
guidance: Forbid downloading and running arbitrary binaries while the extension works.
A justified resource from a well-known independent source is acceptable; it is better to ask the user to install the needed tool themselves.

rules.title: Command or code injection
guidance: `blocking` only if an uncontrolled or unexpected value can really change the syntax of an executed command or code and trigger an action the user did not intend.
Check `eval`, `Function`, dynamic `import` of remote code, building shell strings and decoding executable strings only where a plausible execution path exists.
Parameterized process arguments are not a violation merely because the data is dynamic.

rules.title: Leak of credentials or sensitive data
guidance: Look for secrets in the sources and in logs, sending to unrelated services, and passing to commands that do not need them.
An extension must not read the learners' answers, the attempt log and the app settings beyond what its stated purpose needs.

rules.title: Unsafe or unjustified process spawning
guidance: Name the programs that are started and check that their purpose matches the extension.
Report unsafe spawning and child processes that outlive the app; documented system tools are acceptable.

rules.title: Suspicious or misleading use of the network
guidance: Do not report ordinary API requests that follow reasonably from the purpose of the extension.
Report unrelated addresses, hidden sending of data, undisclosed analytics and tracking, and leaks of credentials or personal data.

rules.title: No clear error message
guidance: Answer views, panels and content renderers must show a visible message when something fails and keep a working state without input; they must not stay silent or break the page.

Do not require handling that the platform already shows to the user itself (for example, the card with a message and “Retry” that replaces a component that crashed, or the note in place of a markdown block that failed to render).

rules.title: The answer view or a panel is not usable with a keyboard or a screen reader
guidance: The component of an answer view must be operable with the keyboard, show a visible focus and have an accessible name; a state must not be conveyed by color alone. The same holds for panels and injected components.
`blocking` if answering is impossible without a mouse.

rules.title: The theme is unreadable
guidance: Check the contrast of text/background pairs: `on-surface` may be left unset and then comes from the base theme by `dark`, so compare `background`, `surface` and `surface-variant` with the text color of the base theme, and `primary`/`on-primary`, `secondary`/`on-secondary`, `error`, `warning`, `success` and `info` on the surfaces.
The threshold is WCAG AA 4.5:1 for text; `blocking` if the main text is unreadable (contrast below 3:1).

rules.title: A logic error gives a wrong result
guidance: Report only high-confidence errors: a wrongly graded answer, data loss, a crash in a typical scenario. Describe the concrete execution path and the observable wrong result.
For an exercise type: `grade` must not accept wrong answers or reject right ones; `referenceAnswer` must pass its own check.
Do not report hypothetical edge cases or cosmetics.

rules.title: Obfuscated, minified, dead or generated code
guidance: The sources must be reviewable by a person. Reject obfuscation and minified code in the repository; report dead branches, commented-out development blocks and unexplained generated code.

rules.title: Behavior does not match what is stated
guidance: Report concrete misleading names, hidden behavior, mismatches with the description, hidden execution and unexplained transfer of data. Vague suspicion without specifics does not count.
